#### A4. Baseline, expected score, procedures, joint distribution and sensitivity

**Source arithmetic (not pace-adjusted):** Geelong PF=376/5=75.2, PA=399/5=79.8, avg total=155.0, margin=-4.6. Perth PF=356/4=89.0, PA=348/4=87.0, avg total=176.0, margin=+2.0. Equal-attack/defence matchup score from these tiny team samples = Geelong (75.2+87.0)/2=81.1, Perth (89.0+79.8)/2=84.4, aggregate165.5, Perth +3.3 before any venue correction. FIBA-40 family median home margin 1.49 from pinned GitHub `COMPETITION_PARAMETERS.csv` is a non-WNBL proxy, yielding indicative central Perth margin 3.3-1.49=+1.81. This is not opponent-adjusted ORtg/DRtg. Independent possessions, pace, offensive/defensive rating numerators, shot mix, 3PA%, turnover/rebound rates, FTA and verified lineup-minute inputs missing; cannot claim a fitted possession model.

**Family prior:** GitHub parameters row `FAMILY_PRIOR:BASKETBALL_FIBA40`: total mean166.65; raw total sd17.93, raw margin sd13.97; family prior is not a WNBL league-only baseline. Since no `Basketball/WNBL` exact league row exists at the pinned commit, exploratory sd(total)=17.93×1.10=19.723 and sd(margin)=13.97×1.10=15.367, with NO sanctioned numeric primary `BASELINE_P`/width-floor certification. Low/base/high total centres 155.0/165.5/176.0 reflect Geelong/attack-defence midpoint/Perth; signed Perth margin 0/1.81/5.5 is a sensitivity span with no fitted probabilities. Default 0.25/0.50/0.25 mixture weights are an *assumption*, not estimated odds. A formal WNBL future study must measure context, dispersion and covariances independently.

**Actually executed exploratory algorithm:** NumPy seeded RNG `202611131849`; 300,000/600,000/300,000 full-match paths; each draws regulation total Gaussian with mean target−0.55 and SD19.723 plus signed margin Gaussian with mean scenario (0/1.81/5.5) and SD15.367; rho assumed0 (unfitted). Score transformation rounds individual scores: Geelong=round((total−margin)/2), Perth=round((total+margin)/2). Any rounded 40-minute tie starts FIBA five-minute OT: each team Poisson mean10.3 points independently per extra period, iterate until a winner. Total OT incidence 2.56% in this exploratory sample. This is a simplified score-level challenger not a full possession/efficiency/stint simulator; 5-min overtime means reflect 40-min pace proxy but are not a measured WNBL OT dataset. No prices, bookmaker moves, live scores or outcome observations used.

| Scenario | n | P(Geelong +6.5) | P(Perth −6.5) | P(Over163.5) | P(Under163.5) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Lower-scoring Geelong control | 300,000 | 66.12% | 33.88% | 33.48% | 66.52% |
| Matchup-centred | 600,000 | 61.81% | 38.19% | 53.75% | 46.25% |
| Higher-scoring Perth tempo | 300,000 | 52.41% | 47.59% | 73.35% | 26.65% |
| **Scenario-weighted** | **1,200,000** | **60.54%** | **39.46%** | **53.58%** | **46.42%** |

**Shadow expected outcome:** Geelong81.62–Perth83.92, combined165.54, Perth margin2.29; P(Perth winner)=55.87%, P(Geelong winner)=44.13%. Normal tail, scenario-centre mixture and overtime make SD of complete distribution greater/different from simple single-scenario inputs. All percentages are conditional, not empirically validated event probabilities or `p_card`.

**Team-score budget at O/U163.5:** if Geelong scores 70, Perth needs >=94 for Over; Geelong 80 -> Perth >=84; Geelong 90 -> Perth >=74. Thus Geelong suppressed scoring alone does not force Under if Perth converts 90+, and a tight Geelong 75–80 score may keep match close with either total. Perth −6.5 requires a 7+-point final gap; winning outright by <=6 does not cover. Overtime can lift Over but narrow/widen the handicap depending on who scores; late foul and bench effects are not separately fitted.

**Sensitivity / width:** low/base/high case shows Geelong +6.5 retains majority *conditional* support (52.4–66.1%) but Over163.5 flips drastically (33.5–73.3%). Observed season scoring ranges overlap, correlated with opponent strength, lineup regime, shot quality; cannot infer safe total from season-average 165.5. Formal exact WNBL reference and adjustment effect table unavailable to execute. League-only numeric baseline attempt = FAIL_NO_COMPETITION_ROW; source first-team scores available but not valid independent historical league cohort. No claim of running `python -m ml reference` or `ml pregame` from the GitHub repo.

#### A5. All supplied lines, W/P/L/V, winner, risk and joint dependence

`GEE_PLUS_6_5`: strongest across low/base/high, because Geelong can lose by 1–6 and still cover; failure if Perth offensive bursts create 7+ gap, late fouling widens. Win/lose (completed, non-void) = 60.54%/39.46% CONDITIONAL EXPLORATORY SHADOW; push=0, void unknown.

`PER_MINUS_6_5`: can win outright yet fail by ≤6, including late narrowing or overtime one-possession win. Shadow 39.46%/60.54%, push=0, void unknown. Raw 3-1 Perth record not proof of covering 7+.

`TOTAL_OVER_163_5`: slight base-case lean; requires >=164 including OT, 80+84 or 70+94 type budgets; vulnerable to Geelong's three consecutive slow home totals. Shadow 53.58%/46.42%, push=0, void unknown.

`TOTAL_UNDER_163_5`: supported by Geelong's home 143/145/147, stronger defensive interior with Han; can fail if Perth's 90+ pace/shotmaking or overtime. Shadow 46.42%/53.58%, push=0, void unknown.

**Joint probability:** P(Geelong +6.5 fails AND Over 163.5 fails) = P(Perth≥7 margin AND total<=163)=17.90% in the same shared scoring paths, no factorised multiplier. Geelong-cushion + Over does not qualify as 2 independent picks. Loss for both Geelong+6.5 and Under163.5 = 21.56%, distinct event, from same grid. Source cards remain non-repository, not officially issued.

#### A4. Coherent diagnostic score distribution, reference/baseline limitations and sensitivity

- **Formal REFMODEL-v1 reference:** NONE; `ml reference tier`, actual release comparison, primary frozen reference rows, hash, and ledger command NOT_EXECUTED. Repositories main read-only and no authorized repository local working tree or writer lease. `p_card` is intentionally NOT_ESTIMATED.
- **Numeric scenario is separate, NOT_PRIMARY:** 600,000 simulated joint team-score games with seed 20261113. Low/base/high mix weights 0.25/0.50/0.25; widths reg-total SD=20.0 and signed margin SD=16.5 points. Team scores reconstructed as G≈round((T+M)/2), P≈round((T−M)/2) with nonnegative truncation. Covariance comes from one joint total/margin draw, not independent side/totals classifiers. Derived team-score correlation 0.190; T and margin latent independent conditional on scenario (an unverified approximation).
- **Base regulatory score centres:** Geelong = 65% × (G season PF75.2 + Perth season PA87.0)/2 + 35% × (G home PF69.67 + Perth away PA90.5)/2 = 80.744; Perth = 65% × (Perth season PF89.0 + G season PA79.8)/2 + 35% × (Perth away PF88.0 + G home PA75.33)/2 = 83.443. 65%/35% are analyst prior choices, not a fitted WNBL weight. Missing possession data prevents credible ORtg/DRtg model.
- **Illustrative overtime:** if tied after regulation, simulate 5-minute OT at Poisson(9.5) points/team and repeat ties; this is an explicit but **unvalidated** OT scoring assumption. OT frequency 0.0230; including OT lifts total mean above unadjusted regulation centre. Margins including OT computed from final team scores. Last extreme tie is resolved at the 9th iteration if necessary. No official OT historical calibration.
- **Actual simulated terminal moments (including OT):** G 80.471 (SD 13.468), P 84.474 (SD 13.141), total 164.944 (SD 20.752), G−P -4.003 (SD 16.658).
- **Regime sensitivity:**

| Regime | Reg. mean Geelong | Reg. mean Perth | Share G +6.5 | Share Over 163.5 | Share Under 163.5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| low | 75.50 | 83.00 | 0.4729 | 0.4090 | 0.5910 |
| base | 80.74 | 83.44 | 0.5879 | 0.5225 | 0.4775 |
| high | 84.00 | 87.00 | 0.5822 | 0.6504 | 0.3496 |

- **Source/assumption status:** scenarios are NOT independent best estimates, not calibrated confidence intervals, and don't integrate exact 2026 WNBL league possessions, true starting-five minutes, FIBA officiating or game-specific play-by-play. The selected Geelong +6.5 lean falls from 0.588 in the base to 0.473 in low, so HIGH_MODEL_DEPENDENCE.
- **Comparator:** PARAMETER family FIBA40 league context mean total 166.65, total width 16.82, margin 12.76 (cross-competition, not WNBL-specific, thus non-operative for player model); same-line WNBL baseline not computed. No adjustment-ledger rows because there is no formal frozen reference and every availability fact is already part of the empirical sample or used only as scenario uncertainty.
- **Monte Carlo precision:** random-sampling maximum standard error 0.000645 (~0.065 percentage points); **systematic model and form uncertainty is far larger**, and cannot be described by Monte Carlo SE.
- **Reproducible local diagnostic:** `wnbl_geelong_perth_scenario_20261113.py` SHA256 `d26a24fd7251084af1b6feac791e30f10b453beb694ef56fc17a04a922280be2`; results `wnbl_geelong_perth_scenario_20261113.json` SHA256 `91599ea319538c1cd5e52061a5cc5f4c7c045d7be2075aaca71de0ef02f21ba2`; latest generated 2026-11-13T18:55:32+11:00. #### A7. Game rules, dependence and counterfactual

- Time 40 minutes, quarters 10 minutes, multiple 5-minute OTs until decided (2026 FIBA basketball rules Article 8; <https://www.nz.basketball/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/documents-corporate-fiba-official-rules-2026-v1-1.pdf>). Supplied full-game contracts use final including OT under BK-OT-1.
- Score-state mechanics: two-way handicap complements have no pushes; totals similarly. Margin can be negative/positive but no ties in final state. The standard score reconstruction maintains point values rounded to nonnegative integers. Extreme totals and blowout tails are normally distributed at a conservative width, but not independently empirically checked.
- **Joint failure (G+6.5, Over163.5):** not computed by the saved current JSON; Fréchet bounds [0, 0.4423]. One mixed scenario can lose both on Perth margin≥7 and low total. The saved calculated 0.2263 is the different joint for Geelong+6.5 and Under163.5 losing together, explicitly not mislabelled.
- Matchup sensitivity: Perth higher scoring raises Over while a stronger G defensive response favours cushion; totals and margins can move opposite ways; don't assume independent legs.
- Pace, minutes, turnover rate, opponent-adjusted ORtg/DRtg, defensive rebounding/3PA and officiating not separately established. No claim of real exact NBA or WNBA-calibrated engine.

### Decision block

**Preferred qualitative direction: Under 179.5 points, low confidence; no strong pick.** Simple opponent-adjusted *scoring-level* checks cluster near 174–177 points, modestly below 179.5, but returning Ellenson and 77-possession fast-paced Wonju games can push above it. This is *not* a reconciled point/possession forecast: published site offensive ratings and implied raw scoring do not match exactly, and the simple average of each pace is an assumption, not official combined possessions.
4. **Low/base/high conditional narratives, not weighted:** low total ~171 if KT slow pace/missing scorer constrains offence; centre ~175–177 with season opponent-scoring and typical pace; high ~181–189 if Ellenson seamlessly restores high usage/DB plays at high pace, KT foreign player scores efficiently, hot threes or extra period. Missing user line vs scenario differences: Under survives 171/175/177, fails 181/189; KT +5.5 survives competitive +1/+4, fails +8/+12.

### A4. Reproducible scenario model, inputs, assumptions, arithmetic and output

**Model identity:** `LOCAL_BPREMIER_SPORTS_ONLY_NORMAL_MC_V1 / UNCALIBRATED`; separate from `ANALYST_PRIMARY_V1` official issue. It is a match-score **diagnostic**, not a league-certified release, calibrator or formal frozen baseline. A B.PREMIER-specific reference tier was not run because this chat has no authorized repo worker/write lease; reference `NONE / NOT_RUN`, `model_p NONE`, `baseline_p NOT_ESTIMATED`. Retired B.League/FIBA parameter rows were **not borrowed as validated B.PREMIER widths**.

1. Inputs from the 16/14 game league records: Kawasaki PF 78.500 / PA 84.6875; Saga PF 78.2143 / PA 95.2143.
2. **Season pairing** Kawasaki E(score)=(78.500+95.2143)/2=**86.8571**; Saga E(score)=(78.2143+84.6875)/2=**81.4509**. No fitted defensive adjustment, only transparent opponent-scoring pairing.
3. **Recent-five pairing** Kawasaki=(71.2+98.2)/2=**84.700**; Saga=(83.6+82.6)/2=**83.100**.
4. **Frozen scenario recipe:** 75% season + 25% L5 = Kawasaki **86.3179**, Saga **81.8632**, full total **168.1810**, Kawasaki margin **+4.4547**; rates not optimized against the requested lines. L10/L15/L20 are checks, not hidden extra weights.
5. **Uncertainty assumptions:** joint regulation total and margin Gaussian with independent axes, SD(total)=**20.0**, SD(margin)=**16.5** points. Neither SD nor zero covariance was fitted to 2026–27 B.PREMIER; these are declared scenario widths. For the illustrative OT correction, regulation mean total is 0.4 lower than the full-game target, integer team scores are rounded, and each regulation tie receives Poisson(8) scoring per team per 5-minute OT, repeated until winner. This is not a validated empirical OT process. Includes overtime; no push possible on the supplied half lines.
6. **Execution:** Python/numpy RNG, `seed=20261113`, **N=200,000 scored draws per scenario**, executed in container before the draft write; code `/mnt/data/b_league_20261113_kawasaki_saga_diagnostic.py`. No GitHub artifact, no ledger freeze receipt. In a single scenario P is wins/200000; the estimated Monte Carlo standard error around 0.5–0.62 is ~0.11 percentage points, vastly smaller than **model-input uncertainty**.

#### A4. Full numeric scenario recipe / comparison with baseline / expected scores
- **Executable diagnostic:** `/mnt/data/bleague_kawasaki_saga_scenario_20261113.py`; JSON receipt `/mnt/data/bleague_kawasaki_saga_scenario_20261113.json`, both conversation-only, NOT repository model code. Seed **20261113**, N=**600,000** (150k/300k/150k cases), self-contained sourced history and assumptions. `scipy` or market input not used.
- Reconcile two uncalibrated strength formulas (both in PPG after possessions conversion): `MIDPOINT: p × (own_OFFRTG + opp_DEFRTG)/200` and `ADDITIVE: p × (own_OFFRTG + opp_DEFRTG − 112)/100`. Population `112` **declared assumed**; no B.Premier league-wide fitted rating. `p`=74.52 inferred possessions; low/base/high pace multipliers `0.97/1.00/1.03`, and MIDPOINT / mean(MIDPOINT,ADDITIVE) / ADDITIVE season-rating reconcilers.
- Small form comparison, not a calibrated correction: recency ΔK `0.20×(71.2−78.5)=−1.46`, ΔSaga `0.20×(83.6−78.2)=+1.08` points; `0.20` is assumption and will overlap season, so **do not treat as an approved adjustment ledger**. Historical league home +0.61 margin split symmetrically: +0.305 K / −0.305 Saga. No extra explicit Dudzinski/Uchio/Araya scoring deduction, avoiding double count.
- Regulation bivariate normal joint `(total, margin)` with total SD `17.66×1.10=19.426`, margin SD `14.94×1.10=16.434`; assumed correlation `+0.08`, not fitted; integer-rounded nonnegative team scores. If regulation tied, add independently drawn Poisson(9.5) points/team in each five-minute OT, repeating until not tied. This exposes tie, OT and tail assumptions, but **does not model actual possessions, detailed free-throw/game-state sequences or player minutes**.
- Three-case mixture `0.25/0.50/0.25` fixed before pricing, low/base/high as follows:

| Case | Weight | Regulation K–S mean | Saga +9.5 scenario | Over 169.5 scenario | Under 169.5 scenario |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LOW_SLOW_MIDPOINT | 0.25 | 83.02–80.33 | 65.92% | 38.34% | 61.66% |
| BASE_BLEND | 0.50 | 87.28–82.06 | 60.23% | 50.32% | 49.68% |
| HIGH_FAST_ADDITIVE | 0.25 | 91.64–83.75 | 53.97% | 62.41% | 37.59% |

- Combined **final after simulated OT** mean Kawasaki **87.526**, Saga **82.271**, full total **169.797** (SD **20.164**), Kawasaki margin **+5.255** (SD **16.556**). No fixed same-line league-only reference was frozen. Historical B League 159.19 total is a stale/possibly mismatched era benchmark and not silently substituted for a current B.Premier calibration sample.
- The Monte Carlo binomial standard error on any combined-row probability is at most 0.065 percentage point at N=600k; this is **sampling precision only** and drastically understates model/lineup/parameter uncertainty.
- Width/input sensitivity across cases: Saga +9.5 **53.97%–65.92%**; Over 169.5 38.34%–62.41%. These are scenario ranges, not predictive confidence intervals.

### A4. Mathematical diagnostic — explicitly not a frozen reference or approved model

To assess all supplied contracts transparently despite missing certified inputs, a **single independent-Poisson regulation score-grid scenario** was actually executed locally; full reproducible code: `/mnt/data/hockey_czech_u20_20261113_diagnostic.py`. This is **not** the repository's NHL release, a trained U20 reference, validated youth-league baseline, fitted goalie/empty-net model or an official `ANALYST_PRIMARY_V1` p_card.

Input rule stated before computing contracts: proxy home regulation-scoring mean `mu_home = 0.5*(Motor season GF/game + Liberec L5 GA/game) = 0.5*(69/19 + 16/5) = 3.415789...`; proxy away mean `mu_away = 0.5*(Motor season GA/game + Liberec L5 GF/game) = 0.5*(45/19 + 14/5) = 2.584211...`. This intentionally mixed season and recent rates lacks an estimated opponent adjustment or shrinkage fit; therefore interpret it strictly as a **conditional scenario**, with high uncertainty.

For nonnegative regulation score `(X,Y)`: `P(X=x,Y=y)=Pois(x;mu_home)*Pois(y;mu_away)`, enumerated **0–36 goals per side**, with probability mass check equal to 1.0000000000 at displayed precision. Full-game shootout/OT tie-branch credits exactly one goal to one side: regulation draw approximately **15.81%**. An overtime-winning goal does **not** turn a regulation tie into a two-goal victory or change either side of the 5.5 total, so supplied half-point contracts have unchanged classification in this minimal branch. Empty-net goals already present in observed historical scores must not be blindly added a second time; a separate event-conditioned pull/empty-net tail was **NOT_ESTIMATED**. Independence, overdispersion, special teams and goalie effects remain unsupported.

**Scenario expected goals:** regulation Motor **3.42**, Liberec **2.58**, total **6.00**; with one credited OT/SO goal per regulation tie, unconditional full-game total approximately **6.16** (side allocation unknown). Regulation masses: Motor wins **55.14%**, tie **15.81%**, Liberec wins **29.06%**. Full-game outright is **not ranked** because OT/SO side resolution is unknown and no user ML was requested.

| Exact supplied contract | W | P | L | V | Exploratory decisive P = W/(W+L) | Official p_card |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Liberec +1.5 goals** | **0.614297** | 0 | 0.385703 | 0 | **61.43%** | NOT_ESTIMATED |
| **Over 5.5 goals** | **0.554320** | 0 | 0.445680 | 0 | **55.43%** | NOT_ESTIMATED |
| Under 5.5 goals | 0.445680 | 0 | 0.554320 | 0 | 44.57% | NOT_ESTIMATED |
| Motor −1.5 goals | 0.385703 | 0 | 0.614297 | 0 | 38.57% | NOT_ESTIMATED |

All half-point events have no push (integer goals). Two complements sum to one within rounding. Score-grid dependence between the spread and total is mechanically present; **joint pick probability is NOT_REPORTED**, since no combined selection was requested. Not a Monte Carlo, fitted league model or cross-validated model.

### A4. Uncalibrated joint score-distribution diagnostic and baseline attempt

A real published `ANALYST_PRIMARY_V1` cannot be built here: no fetched/frozen qualifying reference, no starting goalies, no verified shot-quality/empty-net/OT action model, no `ml/` stage. To still assess the four requested rows, a reproducible **deterministic independent-Poisson score-grid sensitivity**, separately and explicitly labelled `UNQUALIFIED_ASSUMPTION_DIAGNOSTIC`, was computed with `/mnt/data/icehockey_poisson_G0007.py` (**not** in repository).

Illustrative scenario weights fixed before pricing: 25% lower scoring (**Motor λ=3.30, Liberec λ=2.10** regulation), 50% central (**3.75, 2.30**), 25% higher scoring (**4.25, 2.60**). Centres are judgmental shrinkage around the 2026–27 team GF/GA matchup and league total of 6.149; they are **not** fitted to shots, goalies or independent coaching evidence. Goals sampled as independent Poisson with `P(A=i,B=j)=exp(−λA) λA^i/i! × exp(−λB) λB^j/j!`, i,j=0..24, normalized; tail beyond 24 negligible at these means. All directional contracts evaluated on the **same joint grid**, no post-hoc row-specific probabilities. Score covariance set to zero; 5v5 quality, injuries, score effects, special teams and empty-net tail **NOT_ESTIMATED**. Real extra-time tie frequency not sourced; hypothetical equal 50/50 winner of drawn regulation is a winner diagnostic only. On a drawn regulation score, a single OT/SO deciding goal changes an even combined total into its next odd value and **cannot change the Over/Under 5.5 threshold**; −1.5 cannot be won from a regulation tie.

| Assumption branch | Motor −1.5 | Liberec +1.5 | Over 5.5 | Under 5.5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Lower scoring 3.30 + 2.10 | 44.0% | 56.0% | 45.4% | 54.6% |
| Central 3.75 + 2.30 | 48.4% | 51.6% | 56.2% | 43.8% |
| Higher scoring 4.25 + 2.60 | 51.7% | 48.3% | 68.0% | 32.0% |
| **25/50/25 weighted diagnostic (NOT p_card)** | **48.1%** | **51.9%** | **56.5%** | **43.5%** |

Illustrative regulation expected goals: **Motor 3.7625 / Liberec 2.325 / total 6.0875 / margin +1.4375**. Hypothetical extra-time winner goal increases the unconditional final total mean by the model regulation-tie mass **0.1419** to about **6.2294** (no evidence this exact frequency is correct for Czech U20). The Motor full-match winner diagnostic with arbitrary 50/50 overtime is 71.6%. Same-regulation-grid joint failure of both preferred directions (Over 5.5 fails and Liberec +1.5 fails) is **16.1%**; that is an assumption-derived joint metric, not a verified independence or edge claim. Baseline league-only 6.149 mean is context, not a computed qualified `BASELINE_P`. No published probabilities, Brier forecast, Monte Carlo N, or backtest claimed.

### A5. Four-contract assessment and coherent kill paths

**SUPPLIED_ONLY — illustrative order (not a supported quantitative rank):** (1) **Over 5.5 goals** — qualitative slight lean with diagnostic 56.5%, (2) **Liberec +1.5** — weak cushion lean with diagnostic 51.9%, (3) **Motor −1.5** 48.1%, (4) **Under 5.5** 43.5%. **NO_STRONG_PICK / LOW evidence**, because the first row is goalie-, league-, and scoring-regime-sensitive and all probabilities rest on manual assumptions. The 5.5 line is crossed by a 4–2, 3–3, 5–1 or 4–3 game, but lost on 3–2, 3–1 or 2–2 after 60 min if an OT goal produces only five goals. Motor +2 wins can pair with either Over (4–2) or Under (3–1): joint failures not independent. Liberec cushion is killed by Motor's superior offence turning a multi-goal lead into a late empty-net 4–2 or 5–2. A regulation 3–3 with OT winner ends seven goals and always covers Liberec +1.5 if Motor wins by only one.

**Main conclusion:** Do not infer Motor −1.5 from the 5th-v-15th standings gap: in the verified current-season U20 H2H, Motor needed overtime to win by one. Conversely, a low combined total is not guaranteed simply because Motor recently held strong opponents to 0–1 goals. Opponent strength and goalies remain unverified. No derived lines, no sportsbook prices, no EV claims.

**Recommendation:** **Over 22.5 games first (slight/moderate qualitative lean, LOW confidence)**; **Piros +2.5 games second**, Altmaier −2.5 third, Under 22.5 fourth. The order is a risk/robustness preference, NOT an official ranked `p_card` or validated model probability order: model probabilities of first two are close and unqualified, and Piros cushion varies from 51.6% to 73.8% across cases. The Over varies from 61.0% to 62.8% across the **narrow assumed serve regime**, but falls below this if both serve performances collapse. `NO_STRONG_PICK / LEARNING_ONLY`.

- **Supporting mechanism:** both players 2/2 three-set wins in Orléans; combined Piros and Altmaier L10 both have significant extended-match exposure. Indoor court with ~82%–85% hypothetical holds makes close sets plausible, but the hold rates are **not confirmed observations** and are the dominant limitation. The absence of H2H is neutral. Piros indoor Challenger-specific form argues against translating Altmaier's tour ranking into a certain −2.5 handicap; Altmaier's more difficult ATP opponents make the raw indoor W/L comparison non-exchangeable.
- **Over kill path:** a 6–3 6–3 (18 games) or 6–4 6–4 (20 games) straight-sets win by either player, or a very lopsided deciding set following short opening sets. **Piros cushion kill:** Altmaier wins 6–3 6–4 (19 games; Piros −5), or 6–4 7–5 (22 games; Piros −4), including surprise return breaks. **Coherence:** 7–6 6–4 (23 games) wins Over but a Piros defeat by three games may lose +2.5 if Piros is the losing player (Alt wins 7–6 6–4 => Piros −3). Three-set 6–3 3–6 6–4 for Alt totals 28 and gives Piros −2 (Piros +2.5 covers). Both preferred legs often win together on close three-set games; they are positively associated and should not be treated as two independent picks.
- Exact joint-failure for Over and Piros +2.5 (both lose): `0.21016` in hypothetical score states; no bookmaker dependence or market inputs.

#### A4. Distribution and sensitivity, arithmetic

**Model shadow (not primary):** exact recursion over point service probability → service hold → alternating server game states → 6–6 tiebreak → best-of-three set states and completed match total/margin. Each scenario sums all terminal match-score state masses to 1. P(game hold) = p⁴(1+4q+10q²) + 20p³q³ × p²/(p²+q²), q=1−p. Initial server 50:50. Tie-break server order is 1–2–2–2. No point-by-point actual model was run on the official repository. Shadow code under `/mnt/data/tennis_shadow_piros_altmaier_20261113.py` and JSON separately retained.

52-week sourced point win rates: Piros SPW 62.3% all / 63.7% indoor, RPW 39.0% all / 37.0% indoor, 72 all / 16 indoor matches; Altmaier SPW 62.9% all / 69.1% indoor, RPW 34.5% all / 31.1% indoor, 60 all / 10 indoor. Opponent match-up approximation **Piros serve p=½[Piros SPW+(1−Altmaier RPW)]**, vice versa for Altmaier; indoor shrink setting n₀=20 equivalent matches, explicitly *unfitted sensitivity* rather than optimized/validated coefficient.

| Scenario | Piros matchup SPW | Altmaier matchup SPW | Expected games | P(deciding set), shadow | Piros matchwinner, shadow |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All surface | 0.639 | 0.619 | 25.32 | 49.2% | 59.7% |
| Indoor shrink20 | 0.650 | 0.633 | 25.62 | 49.4% | 58.1% |
| Indoor only | 0.663 | 0.660 | 26.21 | 50.0% | 51.2% |
| Two-round stress | 0.611 | 0.673 | 24.50 | 42.1% | 21.8% |

All scenario numbers are **uncalibrated conditional forecasts, not confidence intervals**, likely overstate precision and do not have an independent skill certificate. Point-service independence, unweighted opponents, score-state/pressure, return/serve covariance, retirement terms and break-point volatility all cause error. The most adverse recent-two stress has a much larger Altmaier serving advantage; long-run indoor-only outcomes favor Piros's return enough to preserve the cushion. Because that short-run scenario already overlaps the long-run 52-week sample, it is a **stress test, not a fourth independent piece of evidence or mixture weight**. Formal reference stage, frozen baseline/adjustments, simulation release and ledger verification were not run; shadow does not fill them.

**Expected score:** formal primary NOT_COMPUTED. Indoor-shrink shadow only: approximate expected total and Piros minus Altmaier total-games margin in table above; shadow approximate player games (T+M)/2 and (T−M)/2. These are means across different set counts, not an achievable match score or prediction of a particular final. A 7–6, 6–4 straight-set match totals 23 and meets the Over; 6–4, 6–4 totals 20 and stays Under. Three full sets generally cross 22.5, but early retirement/short decider conventions differ and must be verified.

**League-only baseline:** `NOT_RUN / BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE`, no time-stamped Challenger cohort over identical best-of-three indoor 22.5 and handicap 2.5 was accessed. No retrospective 0.5 substitution. **Adjusted reference:** `NONE`, no official released model or coherent frozen input verified; independent shadow is not a replacement for the formal stage. **Sensitivity:** numeric four-case table above. **Calibration:** no validated scope, NO_DEMONSTRATED_SKILL by tennis rule. **Primary confidence:** low.

**Primary qualitative assessment:** **Over 24.5 games** is the preferred *conditional lean* among supplied directions, **LOW confidence / NO STRONG PICK**. #### A4. Diagnostic calculation, missing primary grid, sensitivity and expected terms

**Dated Tennis Abstract Elo benchmark (9 Nov 2026 snapshot; model input only if admitted through authorised run):** `https://tennisabstract.com/reports/atp_elo_ratings.html?trk=public_post_comment-text`; overall/hard Tabilo 1782.2/1731.8 and Tirante 1756.6/1669.4. Separate surface/overall 50:50 blend per tennis rule: Tabilo `(1782.2+1731.8)/2=1757.0`; Tirante `(1756.6+1669.4)/2=1713.0`; delta **+44.0 Elo**. For a generic best-of-three Elo diagnostic, `1/(1 + 10^(-44/400)) ≈ 0.5630` for a Tabilo match win (Tirante 0.4370) **as a reference indicator only**. This is *not* `p_card`, not a handicap/total probability, not adjusted or certified for post-scheduled timing, and not a model-run result. The Tennis Abstract cached `open` page was stale (August 2026); the current 9 Nov values were visible in its search-indexed snapshot and an independently opened dated secondary page. Fresh-source cutoff and retrieval provenance have limitations.

**Family/coherence:** A properly priced game total/handicap requires a single opponent-adjusted point-on-serve distribution, set-state/tiebreak recursion, explicit two-set/three-set mass, form-shock mixture and full match-losing score states. Those inputs and authorised reference/freeze not available; therefore `DISTRIBUTION_NOT_COMPUTED / BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE / p_card NOT_ESTIMATED / SD NOT_ESTIMATED`. **No simulation, exact recursion, Monte Carlo run, released `PICKS_V2` table or model shadow was performed.**

**Scoreline sanity checks** (examples, not predictions): 7–6 7–5 -> 25 games -> Over; 7–6 6–4 -> 23 -> Under; 6–4 6–4 -> 20 -> Under; 7–6 6–7 6–3 -> 35 -> Over. An underdog who loses two tight sets can cover +1.5 game margin only if total games gap ≤1, not merely because both sets are close; e.g., losing 7–6, 7–6 gives 12 vs14 => 2-game deficit, **Tirante +1.5 fails** if he loses both sets 6–7. A player can lose a match while winning more aggregate games; thus never replace full game states with winner states.

**Sensitivity (qualitative, weights NOT_ASSUMED):**

| Regime | Conditional driving input | Consequence for provided lines |
|---|---|---|
| Close-serve high-hold | Both reach 6–6 often, possible decider | Over increases; handicap may hinge on one break; no numeric p |
| Tabilo first-return dominance | Tirante's second serve attacked, multiple breaks | Tabilo −1.5 improves; Under 24.5 becomes possible on straight-set control |
| Tirante service control / Tabilo disrupted | Tirante wins or holds sets close | Tirante +1.5 improves; Over possible if a deciding set, but not guaranteed |
| Fatigue suppresses one player | Shorter sets and blowout paths | Under increases; preferred Over fails |

No fixed centre adjustment, health probability, form-shock sigma, court/altitude effect size or justified scenario weights from the admitted source snapshots. Three-set share for men's best-of-three population noted in repository `RULES_TENNIS` as approx 0.358 but not applied to this competition as a calibrated match-specific forecast.

For example, Tabilo wins 6–4, 0–6, 6–4: Tirante has 14 games vs Tabilo’s 12 and covers +1.5, despite losing the match. Conversely, Tabilo wins 6–4, 4–6, 6–4: Tabilo has 16 vs Tirante’s 14, so Tirante +1.5 loses. **Tirante cushion kill:** Tabilo wins 6–4,6–4 (Tabilo game margin +4), or any Tabilo cumulative-game lead ≥2; also possible a 3-set loss with uneven sets.
- **Dependence:** chosen first two often survive long/close sets together; exact joint-failure probability in the **illustrative** state tree, `P(Under24.5 AND Tabilo cumulative margin ≥2)=0.239261` (23.93%); that is not a calibrated joint-risk estimate. Do not treat two bets as independent or guaranteed insurance.

#### A4. Distribution, reference and sensitivity arithmetic

**Reference gate not run:** installed repository's `ml.reference` available only in pinned repository code with no local executed workflow; frozen ATP Elo and baseline were not captured from an admitted source at cutoff. Formal `ANALYST_PRIMARY_V1`, adjustment ledger, numerical rank/floor, exact-row league baseline and postwrite pregame freeze therefore `NOT_PERFORMED`. Computations are standalone and clearly separated.

**Exact independent-chain model:** for player T serving on a point, pT=(T own serve-points won + (1−Tirante return-points won))/2, mirrored for player I. For all surfaces pT=0.6515, pI=0.6510; indoor pT=0.6620, pI=0.6750; declared 20-match pseudocount shrink of indoor inputs to all-surface p yields pT=0.65325, pI=0.65722. `k=20` is a sensitivity assumption, **not** calibrated or endorsed by GitHub. Point IID assumption, alternate servers, 6-6 tiebreak first to 7 by 2, match first to 2 sets. Hold probability H(p)=p⁴(1+4q+10q²) + 20p³q³·p²/(p²+q²), q=1−p. All reachable finished-match states enumerated; mass sums to 1. The code computes both totals and margins from the **same** distribution; no normality assumption, no fake 100,000-run claim. 

**Shrunk indoor scenario:** Tabilo hold 83.5%, Tirante hold 84.1%; P(Tabilo win) 48.1% (SHADOW ONLY), P(decider) 50.0%, expected total 26.04, Tabilo margin -0.18. Every half-line complements without push conditional on completed match, all grid state mass 1.000000000000.

**Sensitivity:** All-surface, indoor-shrunk, indoor-only (n=4 and n=7), and ±0.015 point-probability shocks to serve strength; the last two shocks are bounds to test robustness, *not* evidence of actual medical or tactical adjustment. No scenario weighting, no manufactured confidence interval. The supplied handicaps switch preferences under the stronger-Tabilo scenario; Over 24.5 remains above 52% across the listed scenarios but no genuine high-confidence or validated edge. No exact future score is predicted. `BASELINE_P` undefined for source/league admission reason; no misleading 0.5 fill.

**Competition-specific profile:** no validated current NCAA D-I reference release or admitted NCAA team-specific baseline was established in repository `PARAMETERS.md`; tier `NOT_EXECUTED` (no `python -m ml reference tier`, no official `reference run` or `pregame run`). Do not import the NBA/WNBA/NBL constants or state any `p_card` as official. All values below are `LOCAL_UNCALIBRATED_SCENARIO` diagnostics with honest calculation provenance.

**Transparent early-season symmetric offense/defense estimate:** home Rutgers pre-game scoring centre `μ_R=(Rutgers PF 91.0 + Bryant PA 71.75)/2 = 81.375`; away Bryant `μ_B=(Bryant PF 62.50 + Rutgers PA 59.0)/2 = 60.750`. Regulation expected total `142.125`; expected Rutgers regulation margin `+20.625`. **This is not opponent-adjusted**, only direct arithmetic applied to non-comparable schedules, and is especially uncertain in the first week. Box-score pace proxies Bryant 72.34, Rutgers 69.98; likely shared possession environment around 71, not a fitted ORtg/DRtg matchup model.

**Dispersion/score construction:** independently draw regulation `N(81.375,13.5²)` Rutgers and `N(60.75,12.5²)` Bryant points, floor at zero, round to integers. These SDs are declared scenario assumptions, **not statistically fitted NCAA parameters**; combined total and margin regulation SD ≈18.4, score covariance assumed zero (unverified). For any regulation tie, draw independent overtime points from Poisson(5.5) for both sides for each 5-minute period until untied. 5.5 OT points per team is hypothetical, not measured in NCAA, and could alter near-threshold tails. Full endpoint includes every OT under BK-OT-1. Fully completed full-game half lines have W+L=1, P=V=0 in the calculated sample.

**Executed calculation:** `/mnt/data/ncaab_bryant_rutgers_20261114_diagnostic.py`, `/mnt/data/ncaab_bryant_rutgers_20261114_results.json`; NumPy PRNG seed 202611140910; `N=200,000` per scenario; no outcome input. This is a real, executed **chat-local simulation** only, not the repository's production simulator, release, ML freeze or calibration. For p near 0.5, MC standard error <= `sqrt(0.25/200000)=0.001118`, or ≈0.11 percentage points; structural/model error dominates.

### A4. Exploratory scoring model: fully disclosed, NOT the repository reference
- **Independent statistics:** published ORtg/DRtg/pace as above. Model possession count harmonic mean: `2/(1/94.9 + 1/100.2) = 97.47801`. Deliberately shrunk matchup offensive efficiency = `(own ORtg + opponent DRtg)/2`. Neutral NYK = `97.478×115/100 = 112.100`; IND = `97.478×110.2/100 = 107.421`. The factor 1/2 is a **heuristic** shrinkage, not a calibrated TB-2-MD replacement. Any opponent-adjusted model should be validated before publication.
- Venue scenario: add +2.0 pts to home margin, split -1 NYK/+1 IND; central regulation centres **NYK 111.100, IND 108.421**, combined 219.520, NYK margin 2.679. No separate rest or absences point effect, since no measured current cohort effect; risk handled by sensitivity below.
- Probability construction: seeded `numpy` Monte Carlo with `seed=20261114011`, **N=200,000**, normal regulation `Total~N(219.520,18.7²)`, `Margin_NYK~N(2.679,14.05²)` independent; transform `(T±M)/2` to team scores, yielding positive covariance between team scores from total/margin variances. **Illustrative OT**: independent 4.6% indicator, add Gamma(shape12,scale1) total points and N(0,4²) extra margin. This simple OT branch is not rule-accurate on regulation ties; no game-level clock, score discretization, tie trigger or possession state. Normal model can produce noninteger/implausible tails, but extremely small near this centre; half-line proposition is approximated. **No validated production simulation performed**. These inputs and all code are provided in `/mnt/data/nba_nyk_ind_20261114_diagnostic.py` and numeric output JSON.
- Mean simulated full-game scores: NYK **111.39**, IND **108.75**, total **220.14**, NYK margin **2.63**; Knicks outright win probability diagnostic 57.3% (not a user-supplied ML contract). Total SD 18.7 and margin SD 14.05 are *development reference widths*, not prospective calibration for this exact matchup. Normal covariance of total and margin set to zero by construction, not estimated from event-level observations.

**Every supplied contract; common generator, unconditional W/L; P=V=0 by half lines on completed games:**

| Diagnostic rank | Contract | W | P | L | V | Conditional p | Primary reference |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | **Pacers +7.5** | 0.635445 | 0 | 0.364555 | 0 | **63.5%** | NONE; research-only |
| 2 | Over 219.5 | 0.512970 | 0 | 0.487030 | 0 | 51.3% | NONE; research-only |

| 4 | Knicks −7.5 | 0.364555 | 0 | 0.635445 | 0 | 36.5% | NONE; research-only |

Monte Carlo sampling SE at p≈0.5 is sqrt(.25/200000)=0.00112 (~0.11 percentage points), smaller than structural model uncertainty. The results are **UNCALIBRATED_CONDITIONAL_DIAGNOSTICS**, not `p_card`, and neither ML freezing nor documented external-source qualification occurred. Full selection ladder and immutable canonical releases were NOT EXECUTED; only supplied contracts priced.

The largest risk to IND +7.5 is Knicks controlling the glass and Pacers wing defenders unavailable. Possession quality and team-specific pace could change all four diagnostics.
